explanation: RPM mismatch with high vibration indicates wheel slippage.
RPM mismatch without vibration suggests encoder calibration drift, not slippage.
Low voltage plus fast drain indicates a failing battery cell.
High battery temperature is an early sign of power subsystem stress.
Low voltage combined with confirmed power stress indicates subsystem-level failure, not just a weak cell.
Erratic readings with expired calibration is the classic sensor-drift signature.
Checksum failures independently indicate sensor drift/corruption, via a second evidence path.
High current and high temperature together confirm motor overheating.
A stall with no obstacle present points to thermal overload rather than a physical blockage.
A stall coinciding with a detected stationary obstacle indicates the robot is physically stuck.
High packet loss with timeouts indicates a communication link failure.
Position drift without a calibration excuse implies the navigation stack itself is unreliable.
Confirmed navigation unreliability is escalated to a navigation failure diagnosis.
An unexpected watchdog reset commonly invalidates prior calibration state.
Upstream uncertainty reasoning (Module B) flagged suspected physical damage.
Suspected structural damage combined with wheel vibration can also manifest as slipping, via a second evidence path.
Checksum failures co-occurring with comm timeouts often share a common power-subsystem root cause.
Power stress without confirmed low voltage points to electrical noise affecting sensors rather than the battery itself.
